what: Calibration of the disease-target screen's power against the rarity of the disease term.
why: The screen reports a target as 'unjoined' when no document contains both the symbol and the condition. What it actually measures is whether a co-mention COULD occur, and that depends on how often the condition is written down. The same 128-target list was run against five conditions of increasing literature density; the unjoined count falls monotonically. A zero on a rare term is the least informative zero, not the most - the opposite of the queue's working assumption.
method: python3 scripts/disease_screen.py "<condition>" research/pudendal-neuralgia-targets.json --no-ot --out <file>; runs 2026-09-19. Density from scripts/disease_screen.py --density.
caveat: The two title/abstract joins for pudendal neuralgia are both symbol collisions, not prior work: 'AR' matched 'augmented reality' (PMID 38560457) and 'KIT' matched the word 'kit' in a mesh-kit paper (PMID 24217793). A strict join is therefore an upper bound on prior work, not a proof of it.
